name: Catholic social teaching
summary: Catholic social teaching is the body of papal and conciliar doctrine on society, from Leo XIII's Rerum novarum (1891) to the 2004 Compendium. It grounds politics in the dignity of every person made in God's image and in a common good that includes the conditions for each person's flourishing. It defends private property and the market while subordinating them to the universal destination of goods, asks for a just family wage, unions and cooperation between capital and labour, and holds that higher bodies should not absorb what lower ones can do. It opposes both collectivism and unchecked individualism, and takes conservative positions on marriage, abortion and religion while favouring democracy, arms reduction and aid to poor countries.
scope: The magisterial social doctrine of the Catholic Church as set out in Rerum novarum, the later social encyclicals as summarised in the Compendium of the Social Doctrine of the Church (2004), and scholarly accounts of its common-good tradition. It does not cover individual Catholic politicians, Christian democracy as a party family, or liberation theology; answers rest on what the doctrine itself states, not on what adherents might conclude.
